test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Nov, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution:
The correct answer is '**gone**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The sentence is in the **past perfect tense**, which is used to show that an action was completed before another action or time in the past.
 
• The verb **"had"** indicates past perfect, and it must be followed by the **past participle** form of the verb.
 
• The correct past participle of "go" is **"gone"**, making "had gone" the grammatically correct structure.
 
• Other options are incorrect: "went" is simple past, "go" is base form, and "going" is present participle — none of which fit after "had".

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *My parents and younger sister had gone__ to my uncle's house to spend the day.* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• "Went" (simple past) is used alone for completed past actions (e.g., They went to the market).
 
• "Go" (base form) is used with modals or present forms (e.g., They will go tomorrow).
 
• "Going" (present participle) is used in continuous tenses (e.g., They are going now).
